discussion_comments.comment_body: Blocking: this changes the API version on the shared MaintenanceManagementClient, so every existing Maintenance cmdlet moves from 2023-09-01-preview to 2025-10-01-preview—not only ScheduledEvents. The existing scenario recordings still target 2023-09-01-preview, and this PR provides no evidence that the new preview API is deployed in Azure Government/Fairfax and Azure China/Mooncake. Scope the new operation without migrating unrelated commands, or provide regenerated regression coverage and explicit sovereign-cloud availability validation before merging.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Split each Get SDK client method into two separate methods (for all 3 scopes):, Added a throwIfNotExists parameter (default true) to all 3 Get WhatIf SDK method

I think it would be cleaner and easier to review changes if we made a separate SDK client for stacks what-if as it is a separate resource type. This will allow us to see more clearly the new changes and be sure that deployment stacks sdk client functionality is not regressing.

Is there a reason for changing references to gallery to galleryUpdate? I think we should keep the logic as-is (remove the new galleryUpdate variable and just use gallery) to avoid breaking changes, and allow users to still make updates through an InputObject, or through specifying parameters. I believe this change is also what's causing CI checks to fail.

Yes, this makes a POST call, the other method makes a PUT call.

Without a POST call, we cannot remove existing UserAssignedIdentities

A logic error is introduced here now. When Update-AzGallery -InputObject $gallery is used, the InputObject is mapped into the local Gallery variable, but the PATCH payload (GalleryUpdate) is only populated from explicitly-bound cmdlet parameters (via IsParameterBound checks). Since the user modified the PSGallery object directly rather than passing individual -Description, -Tag, etc. parameters, those checks all return False and GalleryUpdate is sent nearly empty.
